observation_summary: The StringUtils.join method throws a NullPointerException when an element in the input array has a toString() implementation that returns null. The code explicitly calls .toString().length() on the first element to initialize the StringBuilder capacity, which fails if that call returns null.
hypothesis: The NullPointerException occurs because the code assumes that calling toString() on an object in the array will return a non-null String. When an object's toString() method returns null, the subsequent call to .length() on that result (or the implicit handling of the null result in the StringBuilder constructor) causes the NPE.
prediction: The code at line 3298 and 3383 will throw an NPE when array[startIndex] is not null, but its toString() method returns null, because the code attempts to call .length() on the result of toString().
experiment_rationale: The stack trace and the provided code snippet clearly show the NPE occurring at the line where the StringBuilder is initialized using the length of the first element's string representation. The bug report confirms that the issue is triggered when an object's toString() returns null. This is a procedural error in how the initial capacity is calculated.
reasoning_summary: The code at line 3298 (and 3383) performs `array[startIndex].toString().length()`. If `array[startIndex]` is not null, but `toString()` returns null, the `.length()` method is invoked on a null reference, resulting in an NPE. This is a flaw in the algorithmic implementation of the capacity calculation.
